lead: I attended **India's first Omarchy Linux meetup** (Omarchy BLR Meetup 001, Bengaluru, 6 September 2026) and presented at the **FOSS corner** — demoing [FOSS Coin]([[foss-coin|FOSS Coin]]), walking through my GL.iNet home router and [home lab]([[homelab|home lab]]) setup. What I brought home was not swag — it was seven builder demos worth stealing ideas from, and a room full of people who run their own infrastructure.

content.content: This was a **community-run** meetup organised by Omarchy users — hosted by **Megabyte** with **Devfolio**, free entry, laptop required. No slides needed: holding up your screen and saying "look at this" counted as a talk. The exact venue was shared after registration confirmation.

rows.Detail: Omarchy BLR Meetup 001 — first Omarchy meetup in India
Show & Tell (themes, keybindings, workflows, agent setups) + Open Session (configs, troubleshooting, next-meetup ideas)
Laptop + power adapter — everything happens on a laptop
Respect every experience level; first-timers ask the most comfortably
Community-run, not an official Omarchy / Omacom Foundation event

content.content: 52 people showed up. The pitch that sold me: **Arch, Hyprland, terminals, keyboard-driven workflows, AI agents** — if those words raise your pulse, you belonged in that room.

I ran a FOSS corner at the meetup: a live demo of **FOSS Coin** — what it does, how the on-chain pieces fit together, and where the project is headed. Then I walked people through my **GL.iNet home router and home lab** — the actual routing, self-hosted services, and wiring that normally lives behind my desk.

content.alt: Explaining my GL.iNet home router to the CEO of LibreDevs
content.caption: Walking the CEO of LibreDevs through my GL.iNet home router setup

content.content: The sharpest conversation was with the **CEO of LibreDevs** — we dug into the router build, what runs on my home lab, and where self-hosted setups are headed. Explaining your own gear to someone who immediately gets it is the whole point of a meetup like this. I also traded notes on distros and tiling window managers with the organisers between demos.

content.title: What I demoed
content.content: **FOSS Coin** (privacy-first SPL token flow) + **GL.iNet router** (home routing, DNS, self-hosted services) + **home lab** (gear and wiring, live). Full write-ups live at [[foss-coin|FOSS Coin]] and [[homelab|home lab]].

sections.title: Builder showcase — what the room demoed

content.content: Devfolio's thread from the day is the real record of this meetup — people showed up with plugins and custom tooling built on and for Omarchy. These are the demos I noted down, in their words where possible, because each one is a project worth following.

rows.What it is: Hyprland workspace switcher with visual previews of workspaces and windows across monitors
rows.Why it matters to me: Think Alt-Tab/Cmd-Tab built around workspaces — jump without remembering where anything lives

rows.What it is: Custom Wayland compositor, UI kit, and desktop experience with per-workspace tiling
rows.Why it matters to me: Reusable components for Wayland apps instead of stitching separate UI libraries

rows.What it is: Browser-accessible Linux dev environment for using a cloud machine from phone or desktop (owns omarchy.cloud)
rows.Why it matters to me: Cloud dev box in a tab — closest thing to carrying Omarchy in your pocket

rows.What it is: Omarchy security plugin that scans installed packages and flags known vulnerabilities
rows.Why it matters to me: LLMs make installing random packages easy — this catches the fallout before it bites

rows.Demo: Fingerprint sudo + OpenCode Go usage plugin
rows.What it is: Reverse-engineered fingerprint-sensor driver enabling fingerprint auth for sudo, plus an Omarchy plugin tracking AI usage so sessions never hit limits blind
rows.Why it matters to me: Hardware enablement + cost guardrails — the two least glamorous, most useful hacks in the room

rows.What it is: Daily-driver Caelestia setup with polished UI
rows.Why it matters to me: Proof that a riced desktop can be both beautiful and liveable

rows.What it is: Omarchy setup running headless on a virtual private server
rows.Why it matters to me: Same dotfiles, no display — Omarchy thinking applied to servers

content.content: We hosted Omarchy's first meet-up in Bangalore last Sunday, led by @megabyte0x. The idea was to bring together people using Omarchy, Arch, Hyprland, and heavily riced Linux setups in one room to see what everyone has been building.
content.author: Devfolio on X, 7 Sept 2026

content.content: IT WAS A BANGER! Many showed off their plugins and custom tooling they are building on and for Omarchy. So many convos around Linux, other distros and how each started with Linux. We kept it intentionally small and it worked out well.
content.author: Megabyte (@megabyte0x) on X, 6 Sept 2026

content.content: That's a wrap for Omarchy BLR Meetup 001. It was a lot of fun seeing the custom setups, plugins, experiments, and ideas people are building around Omarchy. All credit to @megabyte0x for initiating and bringing the crowd together.
content.author: Devfolio on X, 7 Sept 2026

content.title: How I captured this
content.content: Every demo above comes from Devfolio's official thread and the Luma event page — no filler. Original posts, photos, and the wrap video live on the [Devfolio thread](https://x.com/devfolio/status/2096928997997478182) and the [Luma event page](https://luma.com/g4g7r719).

The hallway track was the best part: meeting the organisers, trading notes on distros and tiling window managers, and arguing self-hosting with people who run their own infrastructure. First-of-its-kind energy — everyone there was early to something, and the room stayed intentionally small so conversations actually finished.
